content:
maria: Heads up — Sales asked for a temporary per-tenant header override for AcmeCorp demo next Tue. They want all traffic with `X-Acme-Demo: 1` to route to our low-latency pool. Can we do a short-lived allowlist for that header?

sid: We have header-based routing today but per-org overrides are gated. What's the TTL and how do we prevent accidental global leaks?

maria: TTL 48h. Only requested for two endpoints (generation + embeddings). Need audit log and an easy revoke.

chris: From product POV, we can accept a temporary override but need console visibility (who enabled it, when, reason). Also prefer a canary flag so fallback is trivial.

olivia: Security: Require an approval flow (at least 2 approvers) and store the override in the audit log. No plaintext secrets in headers. Also add a policy that disallows allowlist for orgs with compliance restrictions.

kevin: Infra: technically doable — we can add a route rule that matches header `X-Acme-Demo: 1` + org-id header and pins to pool "low-latency-acme". Quick notes:
```yaml
- match:
    headers:
      X-Acme-Demo: "1"
      X-Org-Id: "acme"
  action:
    route_to: low-latency-acme
  metadata:
    ttl: 172800  # seconds (48h)
    created_by: maria
    audit_id: TBD
```

kevin: But we need a guard: only allow if `created_by` is from an admin group OR request has approval token. Otherwise risk accidental open routing.

maria: Approval token flow sounds fine. Sales can get approvals from security + product.

sid: Implementation plan: 1) API change to accept `override_create` with `approval_token` + `ttl` 2) store override record in DB 3) runtime picks it up and adds header-based rule to routing engine with precedence over normal routing 4) expire/auto-revoke after TTL 5) console shows active temp overrides and who approved.

chris: UX asks: show expiration countdown, ability to revoke, and a simple "preview" link that simulates routing for a sample request.

olivia: Also require that any temp override triggers an immediate telemetry tag so we can filter logs/trace by override_id. That helps audits if something goes wrong.

kevin: One more: ensure the route rule cannot be used to bypass tenant-level quotas. If they route to a special pool, quotas must still apply.

maria: Agreed. For the demo we only need the routing behavior; quotas and billing unchanged.

sid: I'll sketch the API and a minimal console modal. I'll also add a migration to add `temporary_overrides` table.

kevin: I can prototype the engine side — will need a safe mode: if approval_token missing, route rule is not loaded and we log an alert.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/tenant-override-prototype -> staging (sha: b1a2c3d) :rocket:

chris: Nice. Can we also add an internal runbook link for on-call? e.g. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-exceptions — put steps to revoke and escalate.

maria: I'll add the runbook note and loop in Sales so they have the process. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sid: Next actions: I'll open a RFC doc and tag infra + security. If no blockers, aim for a staging demo by EOD Friday.

kevin: ACK. I'll post the proto service logs to the #eng-oncall channel when ready.

olivia: I'll pre-approve for the demo (temporary exception) and leave a note in the audit log.

maria: Great — closing the loop here, will DM Sales the steps.
